title: Request lifecycle anchor and KV stabilizer for async worker propagation
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Introduce a lightweight request lifecycle anchor header and a stable KV-mapping strategy to ensure spans and baggage survive boundary crossings through internal queueing systems, batchers, and long-running worker pools. This ticket implements SDK middleware and server-side request decorators to create a deterministic anchor ID, attach compact KV-stabilizer metadata, and rehydrate trace context in asynchronous consumers while preserving sampling fidelity.
tasks: Design anchor header format and encoding (compact, backward compatible with W3C traceparent/baggage)
Implement SDK middleware: attach-anchor + compact-kv-stabilizer on inbound requests
Server runtime: add anchor verifier and short-lived index for fast lookup
Worker pool consumer: rehydrate span + baggage from anchor and attach to worker-local tracer
Add end-to-end tests: queue->worker->batch->response for trace continuity and sampling metrics
Update docs: SDK migration guide and Console instrumentation section
Create dashboards to surface anchor mismatch rates and rehydration latency
acceptance_criteria: Anchor header is emitted by default in HTTP SDK middleware and in internal RPC clients
Worker processes can rehydrate trace/span identity with <50ms median extra latency
No loss of parent-child relationships for fanout across queues in integration tests
Sampling decision preserved: requests sampled at ingress remain sampled on workers; unsampled do not create sampled spans
Console dashboard shows anchor rehydration success/failure and distribution across regions
decisions: Use W3C traceparent for core trace id; introduce X-Redwood-Anchor header for deterministic rehydration state
Anchor will be 20 bytes base62 encoded (timestamp + 8 byte monotonic counter + 4b checksum) to optimize for indexing and short headers
Store minimal stabilizer KV in a short-lived in-memory index on the host (TTL 30s) rather than full persistence to avoid write amplification during high fanout
Worker SDK will not fetch full context from central store synchronously; it will attempt local rehydrate then fallback to async fetch with non-blocking span creation to avoid tail latency spikes
tradeoffs: Pros: deterministic linking across async boundaries, compact headers, lower central datastore usage for most flows
Cons: small window where anchor index may expire causing rehydration failure; requires conservative TTL tuning
Compatibility: adds a new header; older clients will continue to use traceparent but will not benefit from deterministic reattachment
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Initial design doc created outlining header format and index TTL tradeoffs (see links).
2026-02-25: PoC middleware implemented in go-sdk, local tests for queue->worker trace continuity passed for simple fanout of 1->5.

2026-03-02: Added worker rehydration path and non-blocking fallback; discovered race when a job re-enqueues immediately causing TTL expiry — mitigated by bumping TTL to 30s and adding monotonic counter to anchor.

2026-03-07: Integration run on staging with high-throughput synthetic workload; anchor rehydration success 98.3% at 10k req/s, median extra latency 18ms. Open follow-up to investigate regional spikes (ENG-63210).
2026-03-10: RFC review with security/infra: agreed on header format and in-memory index; security requested HMAC checksum to prevent tampering (implemented).
comments: Ethan Cole (2026-02-21): Left notes on SDK boundary APIs — prefer AttachAnchor(ctx, opts) that returns a detach function to avoid leaks.
Nadia Martinez (2026-02-26): Suggested adding a sampling-flag bit to anchor to handle downstream sampling enforcement; accepted and added to design.
Marco Liu (2026-03-03): Performance review — index TTL tuning seems fine but watch memory growth under extreme fanout. Added memory telemetry to staging run.
Security Team (2026-03-09): Approved HMAC checksum with rotated keys via KMS integration, requested key rotation plan be documented.
Priya Natarajan (2026-03-10): Marking ready for final integration tests; creating dashboard panels for anchor-failure-rate and rehydrate-latency.
